23 July 2026

Monetary policy statement

The Governing Council today decided to lower the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points.

The decisions are based on the assessment that inflation will return to the 2% target over the coming quarters.

The Governing Council stands ready to adjust all of its instruments within its mandate to ensure that inflation returns to its 2% target.

Economic activity

The euro area economy has slowed, reflecting weaker external demand.

GDP is projected to grow by 1.4% in 2027 and by 1.6% in 2028.

Inflation

Inflation declined to 2.4% in May and is projected to average 2.2% in 2027.

Core inflation remains elevated but is expected to decline gradually.

Inflation expectations remain well anchored.

Labour market

The labour market remains resilient.

The unemployment rate stood at 6.4% in June 2026.

Wage growth is projected to average 3.0% in 2027.

Financial conditions

Financing conditions remain tight, and monetary policy transmission is functioning smoothly.

Risk assessment

Risks to the economic outlook are broadly balanced.

Inflation risks are tilted to the upside.

The outlook for growth is subject to downside risks.

Forward guidance

The Governing Council will keep the key ECB interest rates at restrictive levels for as long as necessary.

The Governing Council stands ready to adjust all of its instruments within its mandate.

European Central Bank, 2026
